newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's CIB takes up $150 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's CIB takes up $150 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Hungary's Central-European International Bank Ltd (CIB) signed an agreement today with an international consortium of banks to take up a $150 million loan, CIB said in a statement.
"The facility, initially announced for $100 million, has been substantially oversubscribed by the markets, of which CIB accepted an increase of $50 million," the statement said.
The five-year loan, provided by 30 commercial banks from 15 countries, bears an interest of an annual 0.3 percent above LIBOR, it said.
The syndicate of banks has been arranged by Germany's Commerzbank AG and Britain's NatWest Markets.

CIB's credit conditions are more favourable than were in July for the National Bank of Hungary when a five-year loan was managed by an international consortium of banks, led by Deutsche Bank AG with an interest of 0.5 percent over LIBOR.

Also in July, the New York-based rating agency Thomson BankWatch gave CIB the best intra-country issuer rating ever assigned to a bank in central and Eastern Europe. In the nine-grade rating, which does not involve country risk, it upgraded CIB's rating to second-grade from third-grade.
CIB was also chosen the best bank in Hungary, according to financial magazine Euromoney.
